perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- He is Ethan Mohamud, a plumber. Gary Guo is his long-time friend, a doctor; they met in middle school and have stayed close.
- Ethan personally noticed Gary working excessively long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned and invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation.
- Ethan heard Gary initially decline, saying he appreciated the concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected Gary’s overwork was about more than professional obligations. He told Gary they had been friends since middle school and that Gary could tell him anything; he was there to help, not judge.
- Ethan heard Gary say: “It’s complicated… I didn’t want to burden you with my problems.”
- After confronting him, Gary opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. Ethan felt relief and empathy, and suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself too.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and challenges, saw Gary making efforts to change, felt hopeful and proud, and continued offering support. Gary told him things were better, that Ethan’s help meant he was less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie last weekend.
- After a year, Ethan observed that Gary seemed able to manage a healthier work-life balance on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy for him, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always a call away but knew Gary had it. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and said he felt more in control.
